title: data/runs/<instance>__<workflowId>.json
description: Execution TELEMETRY for one monitored n8n workflow. Machine-written by src/n8n/collect.js. Deliberately separate from data/workflows.json, which is INVENTORY — that file says a workflow exists and whether it is switched on; this one says what it actually did. Two tiers: `rows` is one record per execution, bounded by retention.rawDays and retention.maxRows; `buckets` is hourly counters that outlive the rows and carry the long-range charts and the anomaly baselines.

project.description: An id under content/projects/, or null

tz.description: The IANA zone the bucket keys are gridded in. Bucketing in the reporting zone rather than UTC is what lets the dashboard answer "what happened between 2 and 3pm" exactly, since IST is a half-hour offset. A change here invalidates every stored key, and the collector rebuilds from rows when it sees one.

buckets.description: Hourly counters keyed YYYY-MM-DDTHH in `tz`. Every counter is monotonic, which is what makes the merge in collect.js safe when rows age out from under a bucket.

id.description: n8n execution id, as a string so it stays usable past 2^53

status.description: Normalised from n8n's status, falling back to `finished` plus the presence of an error for instances older than ~1.116 which did not send one.

volumeSource.description: WHERE the volume figures came from. node-data: counted from data.resultData.runData, exact. bytes: n8n reported jsonSizeBytes but withheld the node data, so bytes are real and items are absent. none: neither. An item count is never estimated for a row that is not node-data.

items.description: The primary volume metric: the LARGEST number of items any single node emitted in this execution. Neither end of the chain is a fair answer — a webhook trigger emits one item while the fetch behind it emits five thousand, and a mailer at the end emits one again.

inputItems.description: Items out of the first node to run, i.e. what arrived from outside

nodeItems.description: Sum across every node run. Item-steps, not items

bytes.description: n8n jsonSizeBytes. Present on every execution, needing no node data, so the bytes series is complete even where the item series is sampled

nodes.description: Per-node output items and execution time, in run order. Dropped from older rows by retention.keepNodeDetail — this is the bulk of a row.

nodesDropped.description: Node detail was collected and has since been pruned off this row

checkpoints.description: Item counts for the nodes named in the workflow's `checkpoints`. null means the node did not run in this execution, which is a different finding from 0.

dimensions.description: What was IN the items, where a dimension is configured — counts and pseudonyms only. There is deliberately NO mode that stores message text or free-form content, so there is no flag to get wrong. See src/n8n/dimensions.js.

values.description: group mode: raw value to count, for LOW-CARDINALITY IMPERSONAL labels only — a bucket id, a status, an intent. Capped at 40 values with the tail folded into "(other)", so a misconfiguration cannot become an unbounded dump. Values that look like a phone number or an email are refused outright.

distinct.description: How many distinct identifiers, counted via salted pseudonyms

tokens.description: Salted SHA-256 truncated to 12 hex characters. Enough to tell a returning contact from a new one across executions; not enough to recover the number. The salt is $KW_DIMENSION_SALT and never reaches data/.

repeat.description: Identifiers seen more than once within this execution

tooManyToUnion.description: More distinct identifiers than it is worth holding pseudonyms for, so no cross-execution unique count is possible for this window. The per-execution `distinct` stays exact; the rollup reports the busiest single run rather than a truncated union presented as a total.

missing.description: Items where the field was absent, empty, an object, or too long to be a label

refused.description: Why nothing was tallied — no salt for an identifier dimension, or a group dimension pointed at personal-looking values. Recorded rather than silently skipped, because a dimension that quietly stops counting looks exactly like one with nothing to count.

error.description: One sentence, redacted through src/lib/redact.js. n8n error text quotes the request that failed and that request carries keys

detailTried.description: A detail fetch was spent on this row and produced no node data. Never retried: for an execution n8n has already pruned the answer will not change

dataWithheld.description: Why there is no node data: "too large", "pruned by n8n"

msSum.description: Total duration. Divided by n for the mean; percentiles need the rows and are reported as unavailable once those have gone

covered.description: How many of this hour's executions contributed an item count. covered < n means the item total is a floor, and the dashboard says so rather than implying full coverage.

cp.description: Items through each named checkpoint in this hour, keyed by n8n node name. This is what answers "how much went from Cratio to Meta, and in which hour" — the funnel sums over executions and cannot say when. A checkpoint that did not run contributes nothing rather than a zero, so "the stage never fired" stays distinguishable from "the stage produced nothing".

lastAttemptAt.description: Set on a failed pass. Kept apart from lastSyncedAt so the page can say "last good sync 06:07, failing since 12:07"

cursorStartedAt.description: The incremental cursor, passed to n8n as startedAfter. Newest execution's start minus a minute of slack

truncated.description: Hit the pagination cap; there is more history to backfill
